I've been working this land for 45 years. My body knows what to do, but I still think it through every spring.

**My reasoning:**

My main income comes from wheat and maize rotating on the same fields — that's the backbone, always has been. Quzhou gets dry winters and hot summers, and my well gives me the edge over rain-fed farmers. I'll put about 3.5 mu into the wheat-maize rotation. After the wheat comes off in June, I go straight back in with maize on the same ground. No wasted days.

Cotton is a cash crop and the government still supports it here. I'll keep 2 mu in cotton. I've been growing Bt hybrid cotton for years — it saved me from spraying every week for bollworm. My old back appreciates that. Cotton needs good potassium, and I don't skimp on that.

The mungbean and red bean are partly for the household, partly to sell at the village market. Small areas, low input. My wife handles a lot of that. I save my own seed for these — no need to buy every year.

I'm not going to change things much from last year. At 60, with two people, I can't overextend myself. My priority is steady yield, not gambling on new varieties or cutting fertilizer to save money and then losing the crop.
